title: Blackberry Jam
subtitle: Deep, dark autumn jam from wild or cultivated blackberries
excerpt: Wild or cultivated blackberries give a deeply coloured jam with a full, slightly tart flavour. Lemon juice helps the set. Makes about three 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (Project Gutenberg #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Blackberries have medium pectin, lower than raspberries, so lemon juice is added.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the raw fruit for use out of season — the jam itself is a long-life preserve and does not need freezing.
recipe.batchNotes: Up to 2 kg at once works well.

content.text: Blackberry jam is one of the most deeply flavoured home preserves,  dark, rich, and slightly tart when made from hedgerow fruit. The seeds are small enough to stay in without bothering most people, but if you prefer a smoother jar, push the cooked fruit through a sieve before adding the sugar. Makes about three 450 g jars.

items.prepNote: picked over for any stalks or unripe berries

content.text: Put the blackberries in the jam pan with the lemon juice over low-medium heat. Stir gently until the fruit softens and releases its juice, about 5 minutes. If you want a seedless jam, push through a fine sieve at this point and weigh the purée,  adjust sugar to match the purée weight.

Add the sugar and stir over low heat until every grain has dissolved. Tilt the pan and look at the base,  it should be clear. Do not rush this step; undissolved sugar causes crystallisation in the jar.
Boil to setting point, then jar

Bring to a full rolling boil and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, testing from 10 minutes on. When a drop wrinkles on the cold plate, take off the heat, skim the foam, rest 5 minutes, then ladle into hot sterilised jars and seal.

items.cause: Blackberry seeds are small but numerous.
items.fix: Sieve the cooked fruit before adding sugar. Or accept the seeds, they soften with time and most people don't notice after a few weeks.

items.cause: Lemon juice increased the pectin beyond what the fruit alone would give, combined with a long boil.
items.fix: Reduce the lemon to 2 tbsp next time. Over-set jam still tastes excellent.

items.cause: Under-ripe or fully wild berries are sharper than cultivated ones.
items.fix: Increase sugar slightly (up to 1.1 kg per kg fruit) for a sweeter result. Wild fruit at its best is ripe-sweet in early September.

items.cause: Fruit was very ripe and low in pectin.
items.fix: Return to the pan, add the juice of 1 lemon and 1 tsp pectin, boil again and test.

content.text: 12 months sealed in a cool, dark place. Refrigerate once opened, use within 4 weeks.
